title: Why AGI is pure fantasy.
summary:
**Why AGI Is Still Pure Fantasy** – The talk argues that today’s AI is far from true artificial general intelligence.  Research now follows two parallel paths: (1) incremental upgrades of large‑language models (GPT‑3.5 → GPT‑5), which give ever‑smaller performance gains for ever‑higher cost, and (2) new architectures such as diffusion models that learn more efficiently and handle tasks LLMs struggle with (coding, vision).  

LLMs are limited because they only predict the next token; they lack an internal **world model** of space, time, physics, and causal relations, so they cannot reason about cause‑effect or solve rare logical problems.  They also miss **continual learning**—new training overwrites old knowledge—whereas humans compartmentalize and “reset” irrelevant information during sleep.  

True AGI would require a robust world model, **System 2 thinking** (flexible working‑memory, meta‑reasoning), and an autonomous **goal‑generation** mechanism—none of which exist today.  Even optimistic breakthroughs are projected for 2030‑2040, but safe, globally governed deployment would likely lag until the mid‑2040s, making a realistic emergence around 2050.  

The speaker adds a philosophical layer: we still do not understand our own minds, so translating human intent into code inevitably loses nuance.  Believing AI will solve all deep societal problems is more a coping fantasy than a viable solution.  The message urges leaders and the public to keep realistic expectations, maintain open dialogue, and recognize AI’s genuine limits.
